(p. 451)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Tur (The Mount)

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿By the Mount,﴾ ﴿and by a Book inscribed,﴾ ﴿on parchment unrolled,﴾ ﴿and by the frequented House,﴾ ﴿and by the raised canopy,﴾ ﴿and by the sea filled with fire.﴾ ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is to occur,﴾ ﴿there is none to avert it.﴾

These are the oaths that Allah swore at the beginning of this noble surah. He swore by some of them specifically, and He swore by all of them together in a general verse that covers them and other things.

As for those by which He swore a specific oath, they are: the Mount, the inscribed Book, and the raised canopy. The more evident view is that the Mount (al-Tur) is the mountain on which Allah spoke to Musa. Allah, exalted is He, has also sworn by the Mount in His saying: ﴿By the fig and the olive,﴾ ﴿and by Mount Sinai﴾ [al-Tin: 1-2].

The more evident view is that the inscribed Book (al-Kitab al-Mastur) is the Great Qur'an. Allah has greatly sworn by it in His Book, as in His saying: ﴿Ha Mim.﴾ ﴿By the clear Book﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 1-2], and His saying: ﴿Ya Sin.﴾ ﴿By the wise Qur'an﴾ [Ya Sin: 1-2]. It has also been said that it is the Book of deeds, and it has been said other than that.

﴿The raised canopy﴾ is the heaven, and Allah has sworn by it in His Book in several verses:

• as in His saying: ﴿By the heaven with its pathways﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 7],

• and His saying: ﴿By the heaven of the constellations﴾ [al-Buruj: 1],

• and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿By the heaven and He who built it﴾ [al-Shams: 5].

Al-raqq (الرَّقّ), with a fatha on the ra', is everything that is written upon, such as a page and other things. It has also been said that it is leather prepared thin for writing on. His saying ﴿unrolled (manshur)﴾ means spread out, and from this is His saying: ﴿a book he will find laid open﴾ [al-Isra': 13], and His saying: ﴿Rather, every one of them desires to be given scrolls spread out﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 52].

﴿And the frequented House﴾ is the well-known House in the heaven, called al-Durah (الضُّرَاح), with a damma on the dad. It has been said that it is called "frequented" (ma'mur) because of the great number of angels who worship there. A hadith has come: "Every day seventy thousand angels visit it, and they do not return to it after that."

(p. 452)

His saying: ﴿and the sea filled with fire (al-bahr al-masjur)﴾ has two interpretations among the scholars of tafsir. The first is that al-masjur means kindled with fire. They said: On the Day of Resurrection the sea will blaze with fire. From this meaning is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then in the Fire they will be burned﴾ [Ghafir: 72].

The second interpretation is that al-masjur means filled. It is filled with water. Among the uses of al-masjur to mean filled is the saying of Labid ibn Rabi'ah in his Mu'allaqa (the suspended poem):

They halted in the middle of the riverbed and split it open, a filled spring whose edges were close together.

So His saying "masjurah" means a spring filled with water. And the saying of al-Namir ibn Tawlab al-'Ukli:

When he wills, he looks upon a filled spring, and around it he sees the nabk and the samur trees.

These two interpretations of al-masjur mentioned here also apply to His saying: ﴿And when the seas are set ablaze﴾ [al-Takwir: 6].

As for the general verse in which Allah swore by what includes all of these oaths and others, it is His saying: ﴿So I swear by what you see,﴾ ﴿and what you do not see﴾ [al-Haqqah: 38-39], because the oath in this verse is general, covering everything.

As for His saying in this noble verse: ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is to occur﴾, we have already mentioned the verses that clarify it at the beginning of al-Dhariyat and in other places.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 52, verse 13:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿On the Day they are thrust into the Fire of Hell with a violent thrust.﴾ ﴿This is the Fire which you used to deny.﴾

Al-da'su (the thrusting) in the language of the Arabs is pushing with force and violence, and from it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is the one who drives away the orphan﴾, meaning he pushes him away from his right with force and violence. This noble verse includes two matters:

The first: that the disbelievers are thrust into the Fire on the Day of Resurrection with force and violence.

The second: that on the Day of Resurrection they will be told, as reproach and rebuke: ﴿This is the Fire which you used to deny.﴾ [At-Tur: 14]

These two matters mentioned in this noble verse have been clarified in other verses. As for the latter of them, that they will be told: ﴿This is the Fire which you used to deny﴾ [At-Tur: 14], He, exalted is He, has mentioned it in verses of His Book, such as His saying in As-Sajdah: ﴿Every time they wish to get out of it, they will be returned into it, and it will be said to them, "Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny."﴾ [As-Sajdah: 20], and His saying in Saba': ﴿So today none of you will possess for another benefit or harm, and We will say to those who wronged, "Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny."﴾ [Saba': 42], and His saying, exalted is He, in Al-Mursalat: ﴿Proceed to that which you used to deny.﴾ ﴿Proceed to a shadow having three branches,﴾ ﴿neither shading nor averting from the flame.﴾ ﴿Indeed, it throws sparks like a palace,﴾ and other verses besides these.

As for the first of them, that they are thrust into the Fire with force, Allah, Majestic and Exalted, has mentioned it in verses of His Book, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Seize him and drag him into the midst of Hellfire.﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 47], meaning: drag him with force and violence into the middle of the Fire. Al-'atl (dragging) in the language of the Arabs is pulling with violence and force, and from it is the saying of al-Farazdaq:

؎Noble men are not those who withhold from you their fathers, until you return to a gift which is dragged away (ta'talu)

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The criminals will be known by their marks, and they will be seized by the forelocks and the feet.﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 41], meaning: the angels of punishment gather together one of them by his forelock, that is, the front of the hair of his head, and his foot, then they thrust him into the Fire with force and severity.

He, Majestic and Exalted, has also made clear that they will be dragged in the Fire upon their faces in verses of His Book, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day they will be dragged into the Fire upon their faces, "Taste the touch of Saqar."﴾ [Al-Qamar: 48], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those who denied the Book and that with which We sent Our messengers, they will come to know, when the shackles are around their necks and the chains; they will be dragged, in boiling water, then in the Fire they will be set ablaze.﴾ [Ghafir: 70-72].

His saying in this noble verse, ﴿On the Day they are thrust﴾, is a substitute (badal) for His saying "that day" (yawma'idhin) in His saying before it: ﴿So woe on that Day to the deniers.﴾ [At-Tur: 11].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 52, verse 16:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Burn therein; so bear it patiently or do not bear it patiently; it is all the same for you. You are only being recompensed for what you used to do.﴾

In this noble verse, He, majestic and exalted, mentions that the disbelievers will be punished in the Fire without doubt, whether they are patient or not patient. Neither patience nor impatience benefits them in this matter. He has clarified this meaning in His saying: ﴿They will say, "Had Allah guided us, we would have guided you. It is all the same for us whether we show distress or are patient; there is for us no place of escape."﴾ [Ibrahim: 21].

(p-454) His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Every person is held in pledge for what he has earned﴾. The apparent meaning of this noble verse is generality over all people. In other verses, however, God the Exalted has made clear that the companions of the right (Ashab al-Yamin) are excluded from this generality, in His words: ﴿Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned, except the companions of the right; they will be in gardens, asking one another about the criminals﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 38–41].

It is well known that specification (takhsis) is a form of explanation (bayan), as is established in the principles of jurisprudence (usul).

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

(p-401) In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surat al-Tur

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Every person is held in pledge for what he has earned﴾.

This verse requires the generality of every person being held in pledge for his deeds, even if he is one of the companions of the right, given the comprehensiveness indicated by the word "kull" (every). Another verse, however, indicates that it does not include the companions of the right, namely His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned, except the companions of the right﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 38–39].

The answer is clear: this verse of "al-Tur" is specified by the verse of "al-Muddaththir".

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 52, verse 22:

Allah's statement: ﴿And We will provide them with fruit and meat such as they desire.﴾

No description of the qualities of this fruit or this meat is mentioned here, except that it is "of what they desire." He has clarified the qualities of this fruit in other places,

such as His statement: ﴿And fruit in abundance﴾ ﴿neither cut off nor forbidden﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 32–33], and He made clear in other places that it comes in varieties,

such as His statement: ﴿And for them therein is of every fruit﴾ [Muhammad: 15],

and His statement: ﴿Whenever they are provided with a provision of its fruit, they say, "This is what we were provided with before," and they are given it in semblance﴾ [al-Baqarah: 25],

and His statement: ﴿For them is a known provision﴾ ﴿fruits, and they will be honored﴾ [as-Saffat: 41–42],

along with other verses.

He described the meat mentioned as being from birds, and the fruit as being what they choose over others, and that is in His statement: ﴿And fruit of what they select﴾ ﴿and the meat of birds of what they desire﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 20–21].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 52, verse 23:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They pass around therein a cup, wherein there is no idle talk (laghw) nor sinful speech﴾.

Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr read "لا لَغْوَ" (la laghwa) with the ending fixed on the fatha, and "وَلا تَأْثِيمَ" (wa la ta'thima) likewise, because it is the "la" that negates the whole category (la al-nafy li-l-jins), so the noun following it is built on the fatha together with it. And when it is so, it is explicit in generality. The rest of the Seven read ﴿لا لَغْوٌ فِيها ولا تَأْثِيمٌ﴾ with the raf' and tanwin, because the negating "la" for the category, when repeated as it is here, may be used either in its operative form (i'mal) or in its non-operative form (ihmal). Both readings in the verse exhibit the two possibilities. Its operative use is common, and among the evidences for its non-operative use is the reading of the majority in this verse, and the saying of the poet:

"I did not forsake you until you said openly: There is no camel for me in this, nor a male camel."

His saying: ﴿يَتَنازَعُونَ فِيها كَأْسًا﴾ means: they hand to one another and each takes from the other. "Kas" means wine. Linguistically, "tanazu'" applies to every handing over and taking, so that each people gives some of them to others and hands it to them; thus they pass the cups of drink and conversation among themselves, and this meaning is well known in the speech of the Arabs.

From this usage in drink is the saying of al-Akhtal:

"A drinker who is pleased with the cup kept me company, not one restrained, nor one who dances in it."

"I contended with him for the good wine, the al-Shumul, when the hens crowed and the time of the night-raider's assault came."

So his saying "nazaʿtuhu tayyiba al-rahi" means: I handed him the cups of wine and he handed me them. From its use in speech is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

"When we exchanged talk and she yielded, she bent down a branch with bunched fruit, swaying."

The "kas" is applied to the vessel of wine, and the Arabs scarcely apply "kas" except to a vessel that is full, and it is feminine. His saying in this noble verse: ﴿لا لَغْوٌ فِيها ولا تَأْثِيمٌ﴾ means that the wine of Paradise, which the believers pass among themselves there, differs from the wine of this world in all its attributes. The wine of the Hereafter has no idle talk in it. "Laghw" is every fallen speech with no good in it. The wine of the Hereafter does not move its drinkers to foul speech and raving, because it does not affect their minds, unlike the wine of this world. For if they drink it, they become intoxicated and their minds are lost, so they speak foul speech and raving, and all of that is from laghw.

"Ta'thim" is that by which its doer is attributed to sin. The wine of the Hereafter does not make its drinker sinful by drinking it, because it is permitted to him, so he enjoys its delight, as He, exalted, said: ﴿And rivers of wine, delicious to the drinkers﴾ [Muhammad: 15], and it does not move its drinker to commit a sin, unlike the wine of this world, whose drinker sins by drinking it, and intoxication moves him to fall into forbidden things such as killing, fornication and slander.

What this noble verse contains of the difference between the wine of the Hereafter and the wine of this world has come explained in other verses of the Book of God, such as His saying: ﴿They are circulated a cup from a flowing spring﴾ ﴿white, delicious to the drinkers﴾ ﴿in which is no intoxication (ghawl), nor are they drained of it﴾ [al-Saffat: 45–47]. As for His saying ﴿in which is no ghawl﴾: meaning there is no ghawl in it that seizes the minds and destroys them as the wine of this world does. ﴿Nor are they drained of it﴾: meaning they do not become drunk. And like His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿There circulate among them youths made eternal﴾ ﴿with goblets and ewers and a cup from a flowing spring﴾ ﴿they are neither affected with headache by it nor do they become intoxicated﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 17–19]. As for His saying ﴿they are not affected with headache﴾: meaning no headache, which is pain in the head, afflicts them because of it.

We have already explained the meaning of these verses in the description of the wine of the Hereafter, and made clear that it differs in all attributes from the wine of this world, and we mentioned the Arabic evidences for that in Surat al-Ma'idah, in the discussion of His saying: ﴿O you who believe, intoxicants and gambling are only...﴾ the verse [al-Ma'idah: 90].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 52, verse 24:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And there will go around them young boys (ghilman) of their own, as if they were pearls well-guarded.﴾

He, glorified and exalted, mentions in this noble verse that the people of Paradise will be attended by "ghilman," the plural of ghulam, meaning servants for them. We have already presented the meanings of ghulam and its Arabic evidences in Surah al-Hijr, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said, "Do not be afraid. We give you good tidings of a learned boy."﴾ [al-Hijr: 53].

Here He does not specify what they carry around to them, but He mentions their beauty with His saying: ﴿as if they were pearls well-guarded﴾ within their shells, because that is more eloquent in expressing their purity and beauty. It has also been said that "maknun" means "makhzun" (stored away), because of its preciousness, since the precious is that which is stored and kept safe.

In al-Waqi'ah, He explained some of what they carry around to them in His saying: ﴿There will go around them young boys made eternal, with cups and jugs and a glass from a flowing spring﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 17-18]. In this verse He adds that they are eternal, and He mentions some of what is served to them in His saying: ﴿There will be served to them plates of gold and cups﴾ [al-Insan: 15-16], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And there will be served to them vessels of silver and cups that were crystal, crystal of silver which they have determined in measure﴾ [al-Insan: 15-16].

The apparent reading is that the omitted agent in His saying ﴿And there will be served to them﴾ in the verses of al-Zukhruf and al-Insan is the ghilman mentioned in al-Tur and al-Waqi'ah. He mentions some attributes of these ghilman in al-Insan in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And there will go around them young boys made eternal. When you see them, you would think them scattered pearls﴾ [al-Insan: 19].

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 52, verse 26:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They will say, "Indeed, we were before this among our people, fearful."﴾ ﴿So Allah bestowed favor upon us and protected us from the punishment of the scorching wind.﴾

In this noble verse, He, may He be glorified and exalted, mentions that the people of Paradise will ask one another, and that the one who is asked will say to the questioner: ﴿Indeed, we were before this﴾, meaning in the abode of this world, ﴿among our people, fearful﴾, meaning afraid of the punishment of Allah, while we were still alive among our people. ﴿So Allah bestowed favor upon us﴾, meaning He honored us and graciously favored us because of our fear of Him in the abode of this world, so He guided us and granted us success in this world, and He protected us in the Hereafter from ﴿the punishment of the scorching wind﴾. The *samum* is the fire, its scorching heat and its blaze. Its origin is a hot wind that penetrates the pores, and its plural is *sama'im*. From this is the saying of Umar ibn Abi Rabi'a al-Makhzumi:

*"Fingertips that did not strike the tufts at morning with them, and a face that the samum did not touch."*

The *samum* may also be applied to a very cold wind, and from this is the saying of the rajiz (the rhymed-verse poet):

*"Today is a cold day, its samum; whoever grows anxious today, I will not blame him."*

The particle *fa'* in His saying ﴿So Allah bestowed favor upon us﴾ indicates that the cause of this is the fear of Allah in the abode of this world. What this noble verse contains, that *ishfaq* (apprehension), which is intense fear of the punishment of Allah in the abode of this world, is a cause of safety from it in the Hereafter, is understood from the indication of its address, namely its *mafhum al-mukhalafa* (implicit meaning by contrast): that whoever does not fear the punishment of Allah in this world will not be saved from it in the Hereafter.

What this noble verse contains, both in its explicit meaning (*manṭuq*) and its implicit meaning (*mafhum*), has been clarified in another place. He, may He be exalted, mentioned that happiness in this world and the absence of fear of Allah is the cause of punishment on the Day of Resurrection, in His saying: ﴿But as for him who is given his record behind his back, he will call for destruction, and he will burn in a blaze. Indeed, he was among his people, happy. Indeed, he thought he would never return﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 10–14].

It has been established in the method of *iyma'* (indication by implication) and *tanbih* (alerting) that *inna* (indeed) with a kasra and a shadda is among the particles of causation (*huruf al-ta'lil*). So His saying ﴿Indeed, he was among his people, happy﴾ is the cause for His saying ﴿he will call for destruction, and he will burn in a blaze﴾.

The one who is happy among his people in the abode of this world is not apprehensive or fearful. This is confirmed by His saying after it: ﴿Indeed, he thought he would never return﴾, because its meaning is: he thought he would never return to Allah alive on the Day of Resurrection. There is no doubt that whoever thinks he will not be resurrected after death will not be apprehensive among his people out of fear of punishment, because he does not believe in the reckoning and recompense. That ﴿would never return﴾ means "would never go back" is well known in the speech of the Arabs. From this is the saying of Muhalhil ibn Rabi'a al-Taghlibi:

*"O night of ours at Dhi Hasm, be long; when you have passed, do not return."*

So his saying "fa-la tahuri" means "then do not return."

And the saying of Labid ibn Rabi'a al-Amiri:

*"And a man is but like a meteor and its light; it returns to ashes after it was blazing."*

That is, it returns to ashes. It was said: it becomes; and the meaning is one.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the companions of the left — what are the companions of the left? In scorching wind and boiling water, and in the shade of black smoke, neither cool nor pleasant. Indeed, they were before that affluent, and they used to persist in the great violation, and they used to say, "When we have died and become dust and bones, will we indeed be resurrected?"﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 41–47], because their indulgence in this world mentioned in His saying ﴿affluent﴾, and their denial of resurrection mentioned in His saying ﴿When we have died and become dust﴾, are evidence of their lack of apprehension in this world, and that is the cause of their being in scorching wind and boiling water.

We mentioned shortly before that *inna* with a kasra and a shadda is among the particles of causation. So His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿Indeed, they were before that affluent﴾ is the cause for His saying ﴿in scorching wind and boiling water﴾.

He, may He be glorified and exalted, has mentioned that apprehension of the punishment of Allah is among the causes of entering Paradise and of being saved from punishment on the Day of Resurrection, as the explicit meaning of this verse of al-Tur indicates. He said in al-Ma'arij: ﴿And those who are, of the punishment of their Lord, apprehensive. Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not something to be felt secure from﴾, up to His saying ﴿Those are in gardens, honored﴾ [the verses] [al-Naml: 35]. He mentioned this among the attributes of the people of Paradise in His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who are, from fear of their Lord, apprehensive﴾, up to His saying ﴿Those hasten to good deeds, and they are foremost in them﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 57–61]. And He said: ﴿And the forerunners, the forerunners. Those are the near [to Allah], in gardens of pleasure﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 10–12].

As for His saying in the aforementioned verse of al-Waqi'ah: ﴿and they used to persist in the great violation﴾, meaning they would continue and resolve upon the great sin, such as shirk (associating partners with Allah) and denial of resurrection. It was also said: what is meant by *hinth* (violation) is their violation in the sinful oaths, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they swore by Allah their strongest oaths that Allah will not resurrect one who dies﴾ [al-Nahl: 38].

(p-459) His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So remind, for by the favour of your Lord you are neither a soothsayer nor a madman.﴾ ﴿Or do they say, "A poet, for whom we await the calamities of time"?﴾

In these two noble verses, Allah, exalted and high, negated from His Prophet ﷺ three ugly attributes which the disbelievers hurled at him: soothsaying (al-kihanah), madness (al-junun), and poetry (al-shi'r). As for their claim that he is a soothsayer or a madman, He negated it explicitly with the particle of negation "ma" in His saying ﴿So you are not﴾, and the negation was emphasized by the "ba'" (of emphasis) in His saying "bi-kahin" (a soothsayer). As for his being a poet, He negated it implicitly by the disjunctive "am" (al-munqati'ah) in His saying ﴿Or do they say, "A poet"﴾, because it indicates a turning away (al-idrab) and a denial (al-inkar) that carries the meaning of negation.

Other verses have come negating these attributes from him ﷺ, such as His saying, exalted is He, negating madness from him at the beginning of al-Qalam: ﴿By the favour of your Lord, you are not a madman﴾ [al-Qalam: 2], and His saying in at-Takwir: ﴿And your companion is not a madman﴾ [at-Takwir: 22], and such as His saying negating the last two attributes, namely soothsaying and poetry: ﴿And it is not the word of a poet—little is it that you believe. Nor is it the word of a soothsayer—little is it that you remember﴾ [al-Haqqah: 41-42]. We have already presented some discussion on this in Surat ash-Shu'ara' and elsewhere.

As for His saying in this noble verse, ﴿we await for him the calamities of time﴾ [at-Tur: 30], meaning: we wait for him the vicissitudes of time, until death befalls him from them. So al-manun is time (ad-dahr), and its raybu (calamities) are its vicissitudes in which destruction and change occur. The verification is that time is what is meant in the saying of Abu Dhu'ayb al-Hudhali:

"Do you grieve from al-manun and its raybi, while time does not reproach one who laments?"

because the pronoun in his saying "wa-raybihi" (and its calamity) indicates that al-manun is time. Also from this is the saying of another:

"Await for her the calamity of al-manun, perhaps she will be divorced one day, or her husband will die."

Some scholars said: al-manun in the verse is death, and the use of al-manun for death is well known in the speech of the Arabs. From it is the saying of Abu al-Ghawl at-Tuhawi:

"They protected the sanctuary of al-Waqba with a blow that brings together the scattered ones of al-manun."

Because those who died at that water called al-Waqba came from different directions, so death gathered them together in one place; and had they died in their own lands, their deaths would have been in various lands.

(p-460) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then let them produce a discourse like it, if they are truthful.﴾

We have already mentioned that Allah challenged them with a single surah of this Qur'an in Surat al-Baqarah, in His saying: ﴿Then produce a surah like it, and call upon your witnesses other than Allah﴾ (the verse) [al-Baqarah: 23], and in Surat Yunus, in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Then produce a surah like it, and call upon whomever you can besides Allah﴾ (the verse) [Yunus: 38].

He challenged them in Surat Hud with ten surahs of it, in His saying: ﴿Say: Then produce ten surahs like it, forged, and call upon whomever you can besides Allah﴾ (the verse) [Hud: 13].

He challenged them in this Surat al-Tur with the whole of it, in His saying: ﴿Then let them produce a discourse like it﴾ (the verse).

In Surat Bani Isra'il He made clear that they are unable to do any of that, in His saying: ﴿Say: If mankind and the jinn were to gather to produce the like of this Qur'an, they would not produce its like﴾ (the verse) [al-Isra': 88].

Here, exalted is He, has applied the name "hadith" (discourse) to the Qur'an in His saying: ﴿Then let them produce a discourse like it﴾, just as He applied it to it in His saying: ﴿Allah has sent down the best discourse, a Book consistent with its parts, oft-repeated﴾ (the verse) [al-Zumar: 23], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It is not a discourse invented, but a confirmation of what is before it﴾ (the verse) [Yusuf: 111].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Were they created from nothing, or are they the creators?﴾.

We have already presented the discussion of this verse, and of the verses similar to it, in Surah Maryam, in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Has he attained the unseen, or has he taken a covenant with the Most Merciful?﴾ [Maryam: 78].

The commentary on His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Or do they have a ladder by which they listen?﴾ and the verse [in full]. We have already discussed this verse, and the verses similar to it, in Surah al-Hijr, in the commentary on His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We have placed in the sky great stars and beautified it for the observers﴾ ﴿and We guarded it﴾ and the verse [Al-Hijr: 16-17].

The author: "Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 52, verse 39:"

﴿Or has He daughters while you have sons?﴾

[p. 461] We have already presented the clarifying verses on this in Surah an-Nahl, in the discussion of His words: ﴿And they attribute to Allah daughters—exalted is He above that—while for themselves is what they desire﴾ [an-Nahl 16:57], and in several other places.

Allah's statement: ﴿Or do you ask them for a payment, so that they are burdened with debt?﴾

We have already presented the verses that clarify this and the rulings connected with them in Surah Hud, in the discussion of His statement: ﴿And O my people, I do not ask you for wealth for it﴾ [Hud: 29].

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And if they should see a fragment of the sky falling, they would say, "Layered clouds."﴾

We have already presented the verses that clarify this at length in Surat al-An'am, in the discussion of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And had We sent down to you a scripture on paper, and they had touched it with their hands...﴾ [al-An'am: 7], and in other places.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 52, verse 47:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And indeed, for those who have wronged there is a punishment short of that, but most of them do not know﴾.

The apparent meaning is that His saying ﴿a punishment short of that﴾ refers to what they were punished with in this worldly abode, such as killing and other things.

This is indicated by His saying: ﴿And We will surely make them taste the lesser punishment short of the greater punishment﴾ [as-Sajdah: 21] up to the end of the verse, and His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands﴾ [at-Tawbah: 14], and other verses. There is no obstacle to the punishment of the grave being included in that, since it may enter into the apparent meaning of the verse. What has been said about the meaning of the verse other than this does not appear correct to me. And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.
